30: Get the contents of a file or directory from a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository and a path, optionally with a branch or ref, then retrieves the file content or the directory listing at that path. It is typically used to inspect project files, and it returns the contents or listing found there.
31: Get details of a specific issue in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository and the issue number, then fetches that issue's full record. It is typically used to review a reported item, and it returns details such as the title, body, state, labels, and assignees for the requested issue.
32: Get details of a specific pull request. This tool takes the repository and the pull request number, then retrieves that pull request's full record. It is typically used before reviewing or merging, and it returns details such as the title, description, branches, state, and review status of the pull request.
33: Get list of commits of a branch in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository and a branch name, optionally with paging options, then retrieves the commit history for that branch. It is typically used to inspect recent changes, and it returns the list of commits with their messages, authors, and identifiers.
34: List issues in a GitHub repository with filtering options. This tool takes the repository along with optional filters such as state, labels, or assignee, then returns the matching issues. It is typically used to survey open work, and it responds with each issue's number, title, state, and related metadata.
35: List and filter repository pull requests. This tool takes the repository along with optional filters such as state, base branch, or author, then returns the pull requests that match. It is typically used to review outstanding changes, and it responds with each pull request's number, title, branches, and state.
36: Push multiple files to a GitHub repository in a single commit. This tool takes the repository, a target branch, a set of file paths with their contents, and a commit message, then commits all of them together. It is typically used to apply a batch of changes at once, and it returns the resulting commit information.
37: Search for code across GitHub repositories. This tool takes a search query with optional qualifiers, then looks for matching source code across repositories. It is typically used to find where something is defined or used, and it returns the matching files with their repository, path, and snippet context.
38: Search for issues and pull requests across GitHub repositories. This tool takes a search query with optional qualifiers, then finds issues and pull requests that match. It is typically used to locate related discussions or work items, and it returns each result with its title, repository, type, and state.
39: Search for GitHub repositories. This tool takes a search query with optional qualifiers such as language or owner, then finds repositories that match. It is typically used to discover projects, and it returns each matching repository with its name, owner, description, and basic statistics.
40: Search for users on GitHub. This tool takes a search query with optional qualifiers, then finds user accounts that match. It is typically used to locate a person or organization on GitHub, and it returns each matching user with their login name, profile details, and account type.
41: Update an existing issue in a GitHub repository. This tool takes the repository, the issue number, and the fields to change, such as title, body, state, labels, or assignees, then applies those updates to the issue. It is typically used to edit or close a tracked item, and it returns the updated issue details.
42: Performs retrieval from the AWS Knowledge Base using the provided query and Knowledge Base ID. This tool takes a natural-language query together with the identifier of the knowledge base to search, then retrieves the most relevant stored passages and returns them with their source references for answering questions.
43: Add a reaction emoji to a message. This tool takes the channel, the target message, and the name of an emoji, then attaches that reaction to the specified Slack message. It is typically used to acknowledge or respond to a message without replying, and it returns once the reaction has been added.
44: Get recent messages from a channel. This tool takes a channel identifier with an optional limit, then retrieves the most recent messages posted there. It is typically used to catch up on a conversation, and it returns each message with its author, timestamp, and text content.
45: Get all replies in a message thread. This tool takes the channel and the parent message of a thread, then retrieves every reply under it. It is typically used to read a threaded discussion in full, and it returns the replies in order with their authors, timestamps, and text.
46: Get detailed profile information for a specific user. This tool takes a user identifier, then retrieves that person's profile from the workspace. It is typically used to look up who someone is, and it returns profile fields such as display name, real name, title, and contact details where available.
47: Get a list of all users in the workspace with their basic profile information. This tool optionally accepts paging options, then retrieves the workspace member directory. It is typically used to enumerate members, and it returns each user with basic profile fields such as name and identifier.
48: List public or pre-defined channels in the workspace with pagination. This tool accepts optional paging parameters, then retrieves the available channels. It is typically used to discover where to post or read, and it returns each channel with its name, identifier, and basic settings.
49: Post a new message to a Slack channel. This tool takes a channel identifier and the message text, then posts that message to the channel. It is typically used to share an update or notification, and it returns confirmation along with the identifier of the message that was posted.
50: Reply to a specific message thread in Slack. This tool takes the channel, the parent message of a thread, and the reply text, then posts that reply within the thread. It is typically used to respond in context, and it returns confirmation once the threaded reply has been posted.
51: Convert various file formats to PDF. This tool takes an input file in one of the supported formats, then converts its contents into a PDF document. It is typically used to standardize documents for sharing or archiving, and it returns the resulting PDF produced from the provided file.
52: Recursively crawl websites and extract content. This tool takes a starting URL with optional depth and scope limits, then follows links to gather pages under that site. It is typically used to collect content in bulk, and it returns the extracted text and metadata from the pages it visited.
53: Convert various document formats to plain text. This tool takes an input document in one of the supported formats, then extracts its textual content into plain text. It is typically used to prepare documents for further processing, and it returns the plain-text version of the provided file.
54: Extract structured data from web pages using AI-powered instructions. This tool takes a web page together with instructions describing the fields to capture, then returns that information as structured data. It is typically used to turn page content into organized records following the requested schema.
55: Extract structured data from audio files based on a prompt. This tool takes an audio file together with a prompt describing what to capture, then analyzes the audio and returns the requested information as structured data. It is typically used to pull specific details out of recordings in an organized form.
56: Extract structured data from documents based on a prompt. This tool takes a document together with a prompt describing the fields to capture, then returns that information as structured data. It is typically used to turn the contents of a document into organized records following the requested instructions.
57: Extract structured data from images based on a prompt. This tool takes an image together with a prompt describing what to capture, then analyzes the image and returns the requested information as structured data. It is typically used to read details out of pictures or scans in an organized form.
58: Extract structured data from videos based on a prompt. This tool takes a video together with a prompt describing what to capture, then analyzes the footage and returns the requested information as structured data. It is typically used to pull specific details out of video content in an organized form.
59: Retrieve Google autocomplete suggestions for a query. This tool takes a partial search query, then fetches the autocomplete suggestions that Google proposes for it. It is typically used to explore related search terms, and it returns the list of suggested completions for the provided query.
